data: Overall, this is a brilliant game and I highly recommend it to anyone who likes adventure and story
I love the atmosphere in this game a lot, the soundtrack is amazing and just love the story in general
With fantastic gameplay and a great story, this is a 10/10
it is still amazing, and has some very good graphics
really it is a great game and well worth the full price
way overhyped, lackluster story with lackluster monsters, everything felt like a chore
Out of my 20+ years of gaming, this game has the *worst* control mechanics out of any game I've ever encountered, leaving it almost unplayable

Finally, after years of owning this game, I've stopped being a pussy and finished it.
I'm going to be honest the story was pretty interesting and the gameplay is nice. Even though I always try to check every nook and cranny, I finished game with an item I had no idea where I was supposed to use it. Maybe some day when I'll replay it I'll find the use for it. :D
I definitely recommend this game.

One of the best horror games of all time, Amnesia packs one of the best atmospheres and renders the player helpless, playing tricks both on what it sees and hears. The story and its progression is also amazingly done so that the player will be between hiding in a corner forever or unraveling the mysteries of this place and its characters.

Excellent atmosphere, you have no weapons, various creatures that can hunt you down. But there's also a lot of problem solving, and a great if slightly predictable story going on in the background.
Light keeps you sane, but makes the monsters attack you.
Once I climbed into a room and closed the door, the creature was close, but I thought I got in ok, but then it spawned inside the room and attacked me from behind.... had to change my underwear.

Scary, fun, I don't know how I got through this game because I can't play horror games, but the plot is so intriguing and it was so thrilling I kept going. If you're here you've likely already heard how good this game is so I think it's worth getting if you like horror games.

It took quite a while to get through this. Primarily from lost saves, and neglect. The game is good: satisfyingly interactive across it's world, and navigably intuitive. Manipulating objects in a very analog sense, opening doors, moving objects, all with the mouse. Correlating items to compile tools for various tasks with indirect context to what assembly is necessary. These attributes where defined simply, but adequately, the game is alright, worth a play.

I personally love playing this game. I'm a huge fan of horror but am very easily frightened and am personally not a huge fan of jump scares. This game stays further away from the jump scare horror aspect and they focus more on the creepy vibe. They use their settings to their advantage by using creaky doors, drafty corridors, and damp dungeons. I think anyone who is into horror can throughouly appreciate this game for what it is. A creepy game with an amazing story. And something that sends chills down your spine every time you play it. Overall, a very impressive game. Love it!

I played this back in 2013, high off my ass. It was nighttime, blizzarding out and i had all the lights on because im a $%#$%.

Pretty sure most people would find this a spooky game even during its more mild moments.

Recommend headphones.

9/10

Although not an extremely long game this game is still worth the buy. It's take on the horror and psychological thriller genre was excellent. As you slowly piece together the story throughout the game the monsters hunting you become more and more aggressive. It had me on the edge of my seat and ready to play the next in the series!

The atmospheric world of this game is outstanding. The soundtrack gives the game an emotional connection to the horror and suspense of the scenes. The overall game is well made in terms of its purpose of horror and the frightening journey the gamer must go through.

Are you able to sit in a dark room and play a game where you cannot fight back against the monster and be forced to hide? Then this game is for you! (and not so much for me, spent most of the time hiding and silently sobbing against a wall as Daniel went insane from being in the dark too long)

as an unironic horror ADDICT, i can safely say that nothing has ever caused me so much anxiety and suspense that i havent even completed it in the 5 years that ive owned this game. every time i play it i make about 10 minutes worth of progress. this game is deserving of the most horrifying game ever made, and id recommend it to ANYONE who enjoys suspenseful experiences like me.

This game is beautifully terrifying. Gosh, it has given me pretty awful almost-heart attacks. But I loved it so so much, the environment was so creepy, the scenarios were majestic and I the story is pretty awesome as well! I totally recommend it if you're into creepy, dark and scary as shit stuff.
I'm not fan of quests or horrors, but played this game with a great pleasure. Demo that features athmosphere and gameplay basics is available, so you can try it before purchase.

This is a game everyone should try once, even if you're scared of horror games! I hardly ever played any horror games before but Amnesia does things so well it just made me crave for experiencing the fear it promotes.

A great story and gaming atmosphere makes this a must for anyone who appreciates well made stuff. The price doesn't hurt either since it's by independent developers! Totally worth supporting that team!

This game while it gives me a bit of anoyance when the protagonist wiggs out at the dark and i am A OK in it. is well designed and pretty creepy. I only hope that eventually they will sell some heart moniter periferal so it doesnt act like i should be Absolutely terrified, when i am only moderately excited, this created some disconect that made the game even less scary. over all 8 out of 10. well made, But less heavy insanity mechanic would have made the character more easy for me to pretend to be.

Maybe I'm not the target audience, but I found the gameplay itself to be kind of boring. The horror was definitely there at times but when it wasn't there I was bored. I'm not as big of a fan of horror as I used to be either, which doesn't help.

Beat the game today, 10 hours. If you like Outlast, definitely try this one.

You are Daniel, who doesn't know how to use a gun, can't even hold weapon properly. Basically all you can carry with is an oil lamp to discover a haunted castle and yes, you will be worried, scared because it's dark and you could run out of oil anytime and the sound is scary, even open a door sometimes requires courage.

It's not like Resident Evil or Dead Space or The Devil Within. If the protagonist could shot bullet most games will be end up a FPS game for me. But in this game you can't even hurt any monsters,you have to hide or distract it or escape. Though there aint no many monsters actually. But trust me there are surprises.

The horror feels real. I panicked. The story itself is dark, too. The puzzle solving part is nice, story is legit and if you are careful you don't miss tools must be picked and any notes to tell you the story. Most horror games lack good stories but i enjoyed Amnesia quite much.

10/10.

It's a fantastic survival horror with controls you have to fight with and monsters you hope you don't. Reminds me of old Silent Hill games, and reading Poe or Lovecraft.

Unlike the Silent Hill franchise, this game has a bit more challenge in the gameplay department, leaving you more terrified than disturbed. A splashy, flooded area made me nope right out of the game. That coupled with the sanity management dynamic (hide in the shadows and lose your sanity, or walk in the light and be spotted by an enemy) created too much of the type of stress I'm not looking for.

It may hook you, however, so it's worth a try.

The creatures that wander around the areas are quite terrifying until you get towards the end, since you'll be quite used to it by that point. Overall, it's really good.

I hate to give this a 'Not Recommended', but I don't feel it lives up to the hype.

While I must agree the atmosphere is initially well done, it loses effect as soon as you walk out of a room and there is a..uh..caustic jelly? Maybe? ...all over the floors and walls. Great; someone just turned my horror game into a platformer.

Well, maybe that's just this one little bit; no such thing as a perfect game, right. So drive on. Okay, so.. seek out the x-many components to make a concoction to eat through a particulalry resistance slimewallthing. Back and forth, back and forth to make said tonic and continue on. Not bad gameplay... but not particulalry frightening either.

New level. Alight. Obviously the first bit was just a warm up. Let you get a feel for the mechanics and prep you for the immersion. Right?

Yeeaahh. Not so much. Jump-across-boxes-don't-touch-the-water-throw-a-switch-and-jump-back-across-boxes-to-get-to-the-door-before-it-closes. Or, 'platformer' for short. Not scary. Just try, try again until you get the timing exactly right. Repeated exposure to the same sequence doesn't build immersion, but rather desensitivity. I half expected a big green mushroom to pop out and give me an extra life.

This game is now 15 years old! Living proof that graphics don't matter if the gameplay/experience is great, sound is well made and the storytelling is engaging.

Actually quite disappointing after hearing how legendary this game is. Its not a bad game by any means (It has really good atmosphere and sound design), but the main (and probably only) disappointment is that "optimal gameplay" boils down to crouching in a corner and waiting for an enemy to "disappear". And I mean disappear literally because once they go, they are gone forever. They don't give any enemy a "patrol route" or let them stay on the map (Apart from a single enemy in the sewers) which sucks cause that's way more engaging when an enemy is a constant presence. But instead the monsters just randomly turn up at scripted points, give you a small spook as you run into a dark room to hide and crouch, wait for the scary music to subside and that enemy is gone forever. Big whoop. zzz

Overall great game that immerses you in the story right away with great writing, atmosphere, and unique game mechanics. The combination of the lack of combat and constant battle of not losing your sanity to darkness, creates a sense of helplessness that, surprisingly and uniquely, enhances your experience. The cherry on top is the included puzzle solving elements that are reminiscent of classic resident evil and silent hill games with a physics based twist. Wear a good pair of headphones as the sound design is great and really helps build tension together with the story as it progresses further into endgame.
This game instantly became my favorite horror game, the story, the gameplay, the atmosphere. Everything about this game is quite literally perfect.

A great Lovecraftian tale that gradually unfolds with increasing dread. Your only defense against fear, insanity, and death is light, which I was able to find quite abundantly in the form of tinderboxes which are used to spark the fairly frequently encountered candelabras. Perhaps higher difficulties reduce that frequency. Regardless, there were more than a few nailbiting moments to make this an enjoyable and frightening descent to the end (which comes all too quickly). It is a parts-gathering and puzzle-solving type game, ala Myst, but the puzzles are fairly simple and don't detract from the story. If you're looking for a challenging game to eat up countless hours, this isn't that. But if you're looking for an eldritch tale of otherworldly horrors, greed, murder, and madness, this is worth picking up.

Amnesia: The Dark Descent is a masterclass in psychological horror, plunging players into a nightmarish world of darkness and madness. You awaken with no memory in a creepy, abandoned castle, and the only goal is to survive while unraveling the twisted secrets of your past. The game’s eerie atmosphere is enhanced by its brilliant use of sound and lighting, making every creak and shadow feel like an impending threat. The emphasis on stealth and puzzle-solving over combat adds to the tension, as you're forced to hide from horrifying monsters rather than fight them. If you're looking for a deeply immersive and spine-chilling experience, The Dark Descent will leave you questioning what's real and what's just in your mind.

Amnesia captures the essence of what it is to be terrifying. You're not a one-man army. You're not a space marine. You're not even a guy with just a few hours of martial arts class. You're just an ordinary person with no memory of who he once was trying to uncover the clues behind his past (yeah I know it sounds cliche, but this is one game that makes it work really well). You have only one defense: run. Run as fast as you can and hide. If it's a scary game you want then look no further.

This game is fucking awesome.

Immersive, scary, and dark in every sense of the word, Amnesia: The Dark Descent is everything a horror game should be. Narratively, the game does an incredible job of telling its story through the environment, scattered letters, and sort-of cutscenes. The story is very well-written, and the voice acting is nothing short of real. Every written paper you can pick up, has had a lot of effort and detail put into it; the lore is immaculate, and awards players who seek it. Never at any point does the story feel intrusive to the gameplay loop or shoved in your face, either - balance between playing and telling.

Gameplay wise, you're going to be lost almost all the time, with how obscure some puzzles can be, or that one tiny lever in the corner of the room that made you backtrack for 30 minutes before finding it. This can make some parts of the game tedious, I thought, but nothing taking a short break can't fix. The crippling mechanics of Amnesia play a major role in its terrifying nature; having little to no lighting throughout, or being afraid to use it so as not to get caught, coupled with the fact that you cannot fight back.

Amnesia is not known to be a pioneer in the genre of horror video games without good reason, and I really hope it won't be long until I find another game as good as it was.

Newer horror games have learned all the wrong lessons from Amnesia. What makes a game scary is the feeling of danger, the feeling that something is stalking you and creeping behind you, of never be safe. When a game relies on jumpscares too often, it becomes predictable and not scary.

Scarier than SLENDERMAN. This games has creepy crawlers, rich people, and mental health. It's still scary today and probably will be forever. Its tied with The Bunker for best game in the series as it has no face greater than it's others; the story, gameplay, environment, music, puzzles, and horror are all equally great. Whereas most survival horror games, even other Amnesia installments, fall short in one category or another this one is as close to perfection as the genre can get.
